svg.title: Owner-controlled artifacts through shielded VM provisioning
svg.desc: Five numbered stages proceed downward. The publisher protects a copied template and exports its volume signature catalog. The owner authenticates fabric guardians, approves the catalog, and creates an encrypted shielding data file while retaining private keys. The fabric stages the template and shielding data and supplies approved nonsecret specialization. A guarded host must pass attestation and VM authorization; secure provisioning validates the actual disk and applies owner policy. The owner then verifies guest identity, access, and OS and data-volume encryption.
svg.text: Provisioning: keep secrets with the owner
Follow five stages; each operator handles only its assigned artifacts.

g.text: 1. Publisher prepares and signs
Preserve an unprotected servicing source before protecting a copied VHDX.
Export a volume signature catalog (VSC) for the signed template.
Signing establishes identity and integrity, not a guarantee of benign code.
2. Owner approves and packages
Approve the VSC, fabric guardians, answer file, and shielded VM policy.
Create encrypted shielding data (PDK); retain owner private keys.
Decide which image versions and recovery fabrics are authorized.
3. Fabric stages nonsecret deployment data
Stage the approved protected template and the owner's encrypted PDK.
Supply only approved nonsecret placeholders through specialization data.
Prepare storage, networking, and an eligible destination host.
4. Guarded host performs secure provisioning
Host attestation and the VM's guardian authorization must both succeed.
Validate the actual template and apply owner policy, KP, and vTPM state.
PDK/VSC applicability alone does not validate a replaced VHDX.
5. Owner accepts the deployed guest
Verify guest identity, authenticated access, and OS-volume protection.
Protect data volumes separately and escrow their recovery information.
Retain the original PDK and consistent protected-state recovery artifacts.

svg.text: A visible or running VM is not sufficient evidence of successful protected provisioning.
